deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the preceding pages): X is a space, or topos, stratified by a poset I. There are closed subspaces X_i (i in I) with X_i ⊂ X_j for i ≤ j. The open strata are X_i^* = X_i minus the smaller X_k. For i < j there are 'neighbourhood' spaces U_ij (a tubular-type neighbourhood of X_i in X_j) and U_ij^* (the same neighbourhood with X_i deleted). Together these 'elementary spaces' form a diagram of type Ĩ, which is meant to encode X up to dévissage. This is the 'théorie des voisinages' whose locality was discussed on p.24 (the page labelled 24 in the notes; this is p.72 of 74 in the file).

Case B (p.24): I' ⊂ I is a sieve (downward closed, condition (7)) and X_{I'} = ∪_{i in I'} X_i, a closed union of strata. The map I' ↦ X_{I'} preserves arbitrary unions, sends ∅ to ∅, and preserves finite intersections ((10), (11)), with X_I = X.

This page:
- (a) It states that I', I'', I'_α in those formulas are sieves.
- (b) Case A (p.24) treated a general space X' over X with the pulled-back stratification. Take X' = X_{I'}; the image reads 'X'=X', but the sense requires X_{I'}. Then rather than indexing X' by all of I, which would be redundant, it is more convenient to use the stratification of X' by the X_i with i in I'. The required relations (11) clearly hold.
- (c) The 'parties-cribles' of X' (closed unions of strata) for this stratification, which is the one induced in the general sense of spaces over X, are exactly the traces on X' = X_{I'} of the parties-cribles of X.
- (d) The elementary spaces of X_{I'} are the sub-diagram (12) {X_i^*, U_ij^*, U_ij : i, j in I'}, i.e. the restriction of the Ĩ-diagram to Ĩ'.
- (e) A crossed-out passage combines the two operations. Restricting to an open U' of some X_{I'} would give elementary spaces U' ∩ X_i^*, U' ∩ U_ij^*, U' ∩ U_ij (13). Grothendieck abandons this, and on the next page he instead treats locally closed unions X_{I'} minus X_{I''} for nested sieves.

Purpose: this is bookkeeping for the functoriality and locality of the dévissage of a stratified space or topos into its diagram of strata and deleted neighbourhoods. The point is that the diagram restricts correctly to closed (and later locally closed) unions of strata.
errors: No mathematical error. The identities (10)/(11) and the description of the induced elementary spaces implicitly need a frontier-type condition: X_i ∩ X_j should be the union of the X_k with k ≤ i, j. This is presumably built into the definition of stratification on earlier pages.
The image appears to say 'Si dans A) on prend X'=X', which would be trivial. The sense requires X' = X_{I'} (a slip of the pen or of the transcription).

ideas.what: Closed unions of strata indexed by sieves (downward-closed subsets) of the stratifying poset; the lattice map I' ↦ X_{I'}
ideas.modern_name: Closed unions of strata; the poset-stratified space as a continuous map X → I with I in the Alexandrov topology, where sieves correspond to closed sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in stratified-space theory (Lurie, Higher Algebra Appendix A; Haine; Ayala–Francis–Tanaka)
ideas.where_published: Stratified topoi are mentioned in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6, without this level of detail

ideas.what: Restriction of a stratification to the closed union X_{I'}, with elementary spaces (strata and deleted and undeleted neighbourhoods) given by restricting the Ĩ-diagram to indices in I'
ideas.modern_name: Restriction of exit-path / link data to a closed sub-poset: the homotopy links of a closed union of strata
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quinn (homotopy links); MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie (exit paths)

deep.surprise_reason: Routine bookkeeping: the elementary-space diagram restricts correctly to closed unions of strata indexed by sieves. It belongs to Grothendieck's unpublished programme of dévissage of stratified spaces and topoi, but contains no new result or connection on its own.
transcription_corrections: In line 2 of the second paragraph, the image's 'X'=X' must be meant as X' = X_{I'}.
In (12), 'V_ij^*, V_ij' are most likely U_ij^*, U_ij, consistent with the notation on the next page; the leading symbol is a brace, i.e. the set {X_i^*, U_ij^*, U_ij with i, j in I'}.
'(11) relations' is a margin label; '(11)' refers to the relations of p.24.
'stratification par 𝒰 [?] formée de 𝒰' d'un X'=X_{I'}' (crossed out) probably reads 'stratification sur 𝒰' induite par celle d'un X'=X_{I'}'.
'au sens général des espaces au-dessus de X' is correct; 'sur les traces ... dans X'=X_{I'}' should read 'sont les traces dans X'=X_{I'} des parties-cribles'.
